_comment: Docket workbench config. This folder is portable - copy it anywhere. The working project sits BESIDE it, never inside it. Every key ships with its neutral default; null means resolve at runtime.
_python: null = resolve at runtime: <project>/venv, <project>/.venv, then PATH. Pin an absolute venv path only if resolution picks the wrong one. Spawned scripts do NOT inherit an activated venv.
_transport: sessions: false = today's stateless one-shot path (byte-identical wire). true = persistent role sessions (main/test_spec/review/qa) over a session-capable transport (Option B): one long-lived provider conversation per role per run, opened once, then DELTA turns only; deterministic gates, artifacts and evidence unchanged; a dead session falls back to the stateless path mid-run. Only the headless claude gateway supports sessions today - under vscode.lm the flag is inert (capability-gated). Per-run override: --sessions on|off.
_project: Active sibling project folder name. Set by 'Docket: Select Project' or 'Docket: Clone Project'. null = ask on first run.
_models: These pins are known-good for this workbench's org as of 2026-07. On a different Copilot org, delete any wrong pin (null = resolve at runtime by role); a visible warning + fallback fires on a bad pin - see extension/src/models.js.

governor._max_tokens_per_run: Deterministic per-run token brake (ledger-summed, never self-reported), checked before develop/review/qa/mutation. Over cap = clean halt; --resume continues from what passed. Set 0 to disable. CALIBRATION: the summed tokens_in INCLUDES prompt-cache creation AND cache reads (headless gateway reports the full context size honestly); cache reads bill at roughly a tenth of fresh input, so recorded tokens overstate real spend several-fold. 3M recorded is roughly 800k fresh-input-equivalent. The 800k cap set here previously halted a normal simple ticket (DATACMP-1, 2026-07-30) mid-run at 1.1M recorded and forced two manual resumes.
governor._fast_path: auto | always | never.  The LOW-RISK FAST PATH (mission Workstream D). On a ticket deterministic checks measure as small - clean comprehension, at most four testable criteria, the ticket names at most three files the repository actually contains, at most three owning modules, no danger zone, no forced bake-off - the blast radius and the implementation plan come out of ONE main-agent turn plus at most one batched follow-up read, as two separate typed artifacts through their two separate validators. Live run DATACMP-0-b53bd016 spent nine model calls before development on exactly such a ticket and never reached it. 'auto' lets prefetch.low_risk_candidate decide from those facts; 'always' forces the fused turn and RECORDS which signals it overrode; 'never' keeps every ticket on the separate lead and planner stages. ONE signal is not an operator's to override: a pending plan/plan-change-request.md means a human already asked for a different plan on this ticket, and that always routes to the slow path, which reads the request, feeds it to the planner and renames it .applied. Note the blind-judge bake-off cannot run on the fused turn (it produces one plan), so an eligible ticket forecloses it; with the shipped fan_out_plans 'never' that changes nothing today. A fast turn that needs more than its budget raises a typed complexity escalation and stops - it never silently buys another turn.
governor._envelope: auto | vscode_low_risk | off.  THE VS CODE ENVELOPE (mission Task 16, perf_envelope.VSCODE_ENVELOPE): at most 4 pre-development model requests, at most 35,000 countable pre-development tokens (target 25,000) and at most 75,000 countable tokens over the whole clean path (target 60,000). Tokens here are ACTUAL input + output with no cache discount, because vscode.lm declares cache_metrics unavailable and a discount nobody can measure is a discount nobody should take. Crossing a maximum raises a TYPED complexity escalation and STOPS the run - it does not warn. 'auto' arms it only where it applies: a VS Code transport (by the gateway's own capability document, never by a config key) running a ticket prefetch.low_risk_candidate already put on the low-risk fast path. 'vscode_low_risk' forces it on any transport; 'off' disables it and the run says so. Provider LATENCY is never gated here - Docket cannot promise another service's response time - so the two time bullets (first developer edit within 2 minutes, frozen-test generation and validation within 90 seconds) are proved by perf_envelope.py --simulate-vscode against a declared latency model and only REPORTED on a live run.
governor._fan_out_plans: auto | always | never.  'auto' trusts the lead's risk call - it sets fan_out_plans per ticket and only fans out when there is something to disagree about. 'always' forces 3 planners + a blind judge on every ticket; useful to see the machinery, and to find out whether the bake-off actually helps YOUR tickets - the ledger records which model won each time, so after 20 tickets that is a query, not an argument. 'never' is one planner, always. Plans are ~6k tokens for three; a wrong plan that runs to QA and back is ~200k, so the arithmetic favours fanning out when the ticket is genuinely ambiguous and wastes money when it is not.

developer._note: Bounded repair loops. A repair round re-runs only the failed stage plus a re-review/re-test, far cheaper than a fresh run of five stages. post_repair_review controls whether a repaired stage goes back through blind_review before re-testing, instead of skipping straight to QA - leave true unless you are deliberately trading rigor for speed.
developer._unit_command: null = <python> -m pytest for the per-task unit gate and mutation runs. Set an argv LIST for non-pytest stacks.

comprehension._threshold: 1.0 = halt on ANY unresolved ambiguity and ask the ticket author; lower trades questions for guesses.

plan_approval._enabled: Opt-in human plan-approval gate. When true, the run halts after planning and writes plan/implementation-plan.md with a DRAFT marker as its first line; deleting that line and resuming the run records plan_approval pass and continues into test-spec. false (default) is the old behavior: planning flows straight into test-spec with zero change.

security_snyk._note: Flip on once the Snyk binary and service account exist.

mutation._kill_rate_threshold: Fraction of mutants that must be killed (tests fail against the mutant) to pass the gate. Below this, surviving mutants are recorded as TEST_GAP_FOUND evidence, not a hard block.
mutation._diff_only: true = mutate only lines touched by the diff (fast, focused); false = mutate the whole touched file(s) - slower, catches gaps outside the diff but far noisier.

qa._acceptance_command: null = <python> -m pytest over the frozen acceptance dir. Set an argv LIST (e.g. ["npm", "test"]) for non-pytest stacks.

coverage._test_command: null = coverage run -m pytest. Set an argv LIST for non-pytest stacks.

jira._ac_field_ids: Comma-separated customfield IDs to check FIRST for acceptance criteria, e.g. 'customfield_10300'. null = search: scan custom fields, then rendered fields, then an 'Acceptance Criteria' heading in the description. Jira does not return field NAMES in the issue payload, which is why this is a search and not a setting. Run `python scripts/jira_fetch.py PROJ-110` to see which tier found yours, then pin it here to skip the search.
jira._note: Env var NAMES, never values. Nothing secret lives in this file. Put JIRA_BASE_URL and JIRA_PAT in your environment, or in <workbench>/.local/docket-runtime.env (gitignored).
jira._post_questions: On escalation, post the blocking questions to the ticket as a numbered comment. A question in a log is a question nobody answers - the ticket is where the author already is, and where the answer belongs next to what it clarifies. Docket reads replies posted AFTER its own comment (matched by a run-scoped marker), so old chatter is never mistaken for an answer. Set false to keep questions in the output channel and ledger only.

ledger._local: Relative to this workbench folder. ONE ledger serves every sibling project - the 'project' column separates them, and cross-project org findings come free.
ledger._never_share: Do NOT point this at a network share. SQLite's WAL mode does not work over NFS/SMB and locking there is broken - that is a data-loss incident with a countdown. Events are append-only, so federating later is an export/import, not a shared file. Every run records its origin (user@host) so ledgers can be merged without id collisions.
